messages.subject: Phylogenetic modelling in inla and brms
parts:
I am in the process of switching from brms to inla for some simple phylogenteic analyses, but in simulations, I am seeing some differences between my inla and brms results, primarily, the amount of variation captured by the phylogeny relative to residual variation. For example

set.seed(1)
library(ape)
library(Rphylopars)
library(phytools)
library(INLA)
library(brms)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

cmb_df = NULL
for(a in 1:10){
  print(a)
  sim_data = simtraits(ntaxa = 20,ntraits = 1,nreps = 1,nmissing = 0)
  traits = sim_data$trait_data
  phy_sig = phylosig(sim_data$tree, traits$V1, method = "lambda")
  
  sp_mat_inla = vcv(sim_data$tree, corr = F)
  #Code for making precision matrix copied from https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rspb.2019.2817
  sp_mat_inla <- sp_mat_inla / exp(determinant(sp_mat_inla)$modulus[1] /
                                     nrow(sp_mat_inla))
  prec_mat <- solve(sp_mat_inla) 
  prec_mat = inla.as.sparse(prec_mat)
  
  traits = traits %>%
    left_join(tibble(species = rownames(sp_mat_inla),
                     phy_id = 1:nrow(sp_mat_inla)))
  
  m_inla <- inla(V1 ~ 
                   f(phy_id, model = "generic0", Cmatrix = prec_mat, constr = T),
                 data = traits, family = "gaussian")
  sd_inla = summary(m_inla)
  
  phy_inla = (sd_inla$hyperpar[2,1]^-1)/(sd_inla$hyperpar[1,1]^-1 + sd_inla$hyperpar[2,1]^-1) #Variance captured by the phylogeny relative to the residual error variance
  
  
  sp_mat_brm = vcv(sim_data$tree, corr = T)
  m_brm = brm(V1 ~
                (1| gr(species, cov = sp_mat_brm)), 
              data = traits, data2 = list(sp_mat_brm = sp_mat_brm), 
              chains = 2, cores = 2)
  sm_brm = summary(m_brm)
  phy_brm = (sm_brm$random[[1]][1,1]^2)/(sm_brm$spec_pars[1,1]^2 + sm_brm$random[[1]][1,1]^2) #Variance captured by the phylogeny relative to the residual error variance
  
  df = data.frame(
    run = a,
    phy_sig = phy_sig[[1]],
    phy_inla,
    phy_brm
  )
  cmb_df = rbind(cmb_df, df)
}

ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = cmb_df,
             aes(x = phy_brm, y = phy_inla)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.9, 1), ylim = c(0.9, 1)) 

If both inla and brms were producing the same model, I would expect these points to fall on a straight line where beta = 1

Am I missing something obvious in my inla code? Or is it an interpretation issue?

P.S. I have used default priors for both inla and brms.

Tom

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Phylogenetic modelling in inla and brms
parts:
Hi THomas,

since the default priors are sure to be different in the different systems, that would be my first place to look...
Default priors really only exist to make coding faster in cases where the priors only have a minor influence, but in cases where the priors do matter, one needs to be more careful (and arguably, one needs to be careful also when the priors don't matter, since we usually don't know if they matter or not until we check!)

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Phylogenetic modelling in inla and brms
parts:
Another issue is that for inla, you're using E(prec)^-1 in the calculation of phy_inla, but in phy_brms, you're using E(std.dev)^2, which is not the same quantity unless there is no posterior uncertainty in the precision parameter.

Finn

parts:
Computing the inla-equivalent of the estimator you used on the brms output,

  hyp <- inla.hyperpar.sample(n = 1000, result = m_inla)
  phy_inla_like_brm = mean(hyp[,2]^-0.5)^2 / sum(colMeans(hyp^-0.5)^2)

does bring the values closer together in some of the simulations, but it seems the precision/std.dev. estimates are generally different, and I would start by looking at the priors.

Finn
